The '''2017–18 Primeira Liga''' (also known as '''Liga NOS''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 84th season of the [[Primeira Liga]], the top professional league for Portuguese [[association football]] clubs. [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] were the defending champions for a fourth consecutive time, but they did not retain the title. [[FC Porto|Porto]] became the new champions with two matches to spare, clinching their 28th league title. This was their first trophy in four years.

Since Portugal dropped from fifth to seventh place in the [[UEFA coefficient#League coefficient|UEFA association coefficient rankings]] at the end of 2016–17 season, only the two best-ranked teams could qualify for the [[UEFA Champions League]] (the champions entered directly into the group stage, and the runners-up entered the third qualifying round). The third and fourth-placed teams qualified respectively to the [[UEFA Europa League]] third and second qualifying rounds.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grad |first=Futbol |date=2017-03-17 |title=Russia's UEFA Coefficients Glory is Overshadowed by Uncertainty of Rule Changes |url=https://www.futbolgrad.com/russias-uefa-coefficients-rule-changes/ |access-date=2023-06-05 |website=Futbolgrad |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |date=2017-03-22 |title=Top six in UEFA association club rankings confirmed |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0237-0e9689d7de66-bfe4897e99b5-1000--top-six-in-uefa-association-club-rankings-confirmed/ |access-date=2023-06-05 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Teams==
Eighteen teams competed in the league – the top sixteen teams from the [[2016–17 Primeira Liga|2016–17 season]], as well as two teams promoted from the [[2016–17 LigaPro|LigaPro]].

[[Portimonense S.C.|Portimonense]] became the first club to be promoted on 23 April 2017 and will play in Primeira Liga for the first time since the [[2010–11 Primeira Liga|2010–11 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://observador.pt/2017/04/23/portimonense-sobe-a-i-liga-apos-derrota-do-varzim/|title=Portimonense sobe à I Liga, após derrota do Varzim |trans-title=Portimonense promoted to Primeira Liga after Varzim's defeat|website=Observador|language=pt|date=23 April 2017|access-date=21 May 2017}}</ref> On 21 May 2017, after a 2–1 win in Azores against [[C.D. Santa Clara|Santa Clara]], they were crowned champions.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/segunda_liga/artigo/2017/05/21/portimonense-e-o-campeao-da-ii-liga|title=Portimonense é o campeão da II Liga|trans-title=Portimonense are Segunda Liga's new champions|website=Sapo Desporto |language=pt|date=23 April 2017|access-date=21 May 2017}}</ref> The other team promoted were runners-up [[C.D. Aves|Desportivo das Aves]], following a 2–2 draw against [[União da Madeira]] on 30 April 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.jn.pt/desporto/interior/desportivo-das-aves-sobe-a-i-liga-6256603.html|title=Desportivo das Aves sobe à I Liga|trans-title=Desportivo das Aves promoted to Primeira Liga|website=[[Jornal de Notícias|JN]]|language=pt|date=30 April 2017|access-date=21 May 2017}}</ref> This will mark the return of the Vila das Aves' team to the top flight after a 10-season absence.

The two promoted clubs replaced [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]] and [[F.C. Arouca|Arouca]]. Nacional confirmed their relegation on 5 May 2017, 15 years after their promotion, when [[Moreirense F.C.|Moreirense]], who were also struggling to escape relegation, beat [[S.C. Braga|Braga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.zerozero.pt/news.php?id=195725|title=15 anos depois, o Nacional despede-se da Liga. "Adeus" ou "até já"?|trans-title=15 years later, Nacional says goodbye to Liga. «Farewell» or «See you soon»?|website=zerozero |language=pt|date=5 May 2017|access-date=21 May 2017}}</ref> On the last matchday, Arouca's 4–2 defeat against [[G.D. Estoril Praia|Estoril]] sealed their relegation, four seasons after having been promoted for the first time to Primeira Liga.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/primeira_liga/artigo/2017/05/21/arouca-desce-de-divisao|title=Arouca perde no Estoril e desce à segunda divisão|trans-title=Arouca loses in Estoril and are relegated do second division|website=Sapo Desporto |language=pt|date=21 May 2017|access-date=21 May 2017}}</ref>

===Annual awards===

==== Liga Portugal ====
===== Player of the Season =====
The Player of the Season was awarded to {{flagicon|POR}} [[Bruno Fernandes (footballer, born 1994)|Bruno Fernandes]] ([[Sporting CP]]).<ref name="Liga Portugal">{{Cite news|url=https://ligaportugal.pt/pt/epocas/20182019/noticias/geral/bruno-fernandes-eleito-melhor-jogador-da-liga-nos/|title=Bruno Fernandes eleito Melhor Jogador da Liga NOS|work=Liga Portugal|access-date=2018-07-08}}</ref>

===== Manager of the Season =====
The Manager of the Season was awarded to {{flagicon|POR}} [[Sérgio Conceição]] ([[FC Porto|Porto]]).<ref name="Liga Portugal" />

===== Goal of the Season =====
The Goal of the Season was awarded to {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Rodrigo Pinho]] ([[C.S. Marítimo|Marítimo]]), against [[C.D. Tondela|Tondela]] on 28 October 2017.<ref name="Liga Portugal" />
